messages:
maria: P0 alert - continuous-batcher queue growth in us-east-1. Multiple GPU OOMs, a few containers crashed, one node flapped. Paging observed on nodes with 24GB cards. Investigating. :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Incident triggered by rule `continuous-batcher.high_queue_growth` in prod-us-east at 2025-11-07T02:14:59Z. Pager duty group paged: eng-oncall.
ashish: I'm looking. Can you paste the deploy/job id if any?
maria: No new deploys in the last hour. Last rollout was yesterday. This looks like runtime batch growth.
priya: Observed sustained queue depth > 6k on the batch queue, latency tail spiking to > 30s for many requests. Some GPUs showing > 20GB memory usage with kernel OOM.
kevin: Can you run `kubectl top pods -n redwood-inference --containers` and `nvidia-smi` on one of the affected nodes?
maria: Pasting quick outputs: ```
$ kubectl top pods -n redwood-inference --containers
continuous-batcher-7f4c  1500m  23Gi
continuous-batcher-9a2d  2000m  24Gi
kv-cache-0              100m   1Gi
```
and `nvidia-smi` shows processes pinned to the batcher with growing memory footprint.
ashish: That matches a batching loop that stopped emitting batches and kept enqueuing. Could be deadlock or missing flush.
priya: I can attach pstack/ltrace to a crashed container if it's still alive. Any customers calling long sequences?
mevan: CS - we have a few high-traffic customers hitting embeddings/rerank endpoints from the east region. They're seeing 503s and huge latencies. One customer reported a timeout at 02:12 UTC.
maria: Initial mitigation ideas: 1) disable continuous batching in prod-us-east as a config override, 2) fallback route new requests to smaller model variant to reduce memory pressure, 3) drain worst nodes.
kevin: Agreed. Priya, can you prepare the override? Ashish, can you handle node drains?
priya: I'll patch the runtime config: set `continuous_batching.enabled=false` via the config manager for us-east pool. Command: ```curl -X POST https://internal-config/overrides -d '{"pool":"us-east","continuous_batching":false}'``` Doing a dry-run then apply.
deploy-bot: Config change requested by priya: `continuous_batching=false` for pool=us-east. Waiting approvals...
maria: Approving. :thumbsup:
ashish: I'm going to trigger the routing fallback: route traffic for endpoints `text.generate` and `chat.stream` to `redwood/gptx-small-v1` for the us-east region only. That halves GPU footprint.
ops-bot: Routing policy `fallback-small-model` created and applied to pool=us-east.
kevin: Ashish - please cordon and drain node ip-10-2-5-18, it had 3 container crashes. Use `kubectl drain ip-10-2-5-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
ashish: Node cordoned. Draining now. Noticing one pod stuck in terminating - investigating.
priya: After disabling batching and applying fallback, I'm seeing queue depth drop in ~90s and p99 latency dropping from 31s to ~4s. Memory usage on some cards dropped to ~6-8GB.
maria: Good. Any residual OOMs?
kevin: No new OOM reports in the last 3 minutes. The stuck pod was due to a kernel loop waiting on nvlink; force kill resolved it.
ashish: There's a suspicious pattern in the batcher logs - repeated `enqueue()` successes but no `flush()` calls for certain long-running requests. Snippet: ```[2025-11-07T02:09:12Z] batcher: enqueue req=0x7f9aef size=1024
[2025-11-07T02:09:12Z] batcher: enqueue req=0x7f9aef size=2048
...
# no flush for 28s
```
priya: That points to a deadlock at the batcher flush path. We'll need a code patch to add a soft cap/wakeup on enqueues. For now the config off is fine.
mevan: Customer impact: We're seeing 12 impacted customers with >5% error rate in us-east, one enterprise (acme-co) at 18% errors. CS is notifying them, setting expectations.
maria: Opening incident ticket INC-2025-11107-batcher-us-east. Severity P0. Timeline: 02:14 - alert; 02:18 - billing routing fallback; 02:22 - batching disabled; 02:24 - p99 latency reduced; 02:30 - node drains completed.
kevin: Postmortem owners: priya (runtime), ashish (release fix), kevin (SRE / rollout plan).
ashish: For the immediate code fix I'll add a guard: if queue_size > 2048 then force a flush and backpressure incoming requests with 429s. Also adding instrumentation to emit `enqueue_no_flush_count`.
priya: I'll push a hotpatch to a canary pool and validate for 1 hour before rolling. Code snippet: ```if (queue.size() > SOFT_CAP) { trigger_flush(); set_backpressure(); }```
maria: We need comms. Evan - can you prepare a status page blurb and CS template? Mention that we've applied failover and are working on a root cause fix.
mevan: Drafting now. ETA 10 minutes. I'll include affected endpoints and estimated recovery window ~2 hours for full rollout.
kevin: Also escalate to infra for possible node firmware/driver issues since we saw nvlink hangs. Opened ticket INF-4242.
ashish: Noting: may also be exacerbated by a recent config that increased per-request token budget for rerank. Will check config diff.
priya: One more diagnostic: captured core dump from container. Uploading stack trace to the incident folder: `s3://redwood-incidents/1839999999/cores/`
maria: OK team — time for handoff to night-shift. I'll do a brief for the next oncall: Kevin will be primary. Keep batching disabled in us-east until after the hotpatch verification.
kevin: Taking over. Handoff notes: batching disabled, fallback model routing in place, drained one flapping node, patch in progress for soft cap + backpressure, CS notified. Pagerduty escalation window set to 15m.
ashish: Leaving my debug logs and a reproducer in the incident folder. Will join if needed.
mevan: Status page posted at 02:40 UTC: "Investigating - degraded performance for inference in us-east. Failover applied. We will update."
kevin: Thanks everyone. Next steps: priya to complete hotpatch + canary by 04:00, ashish to prepare a safe rollout plan with rollback steps, CS to watch customer error rates and inform top 5. Postmortem due in 3 days.
priya: Will push canary at 03:10 and report metrics at 03:25.
maria: Appreciate the quick response. Closing active coordination here, will update if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
